resources.string: This service provides information based on the Korean government\'s Digital Twin National Land data. Users are responsible for actual flight permits and safety.

DronePass is
an integrated management app
that provides all the information you need for drone flight.

Check flight zones, real-time weather, KP index,
and sunrise/sunset times all at once.
Display drone flight permitted areas on map
Automatic notification 7 days before flight end date
Wind direction, speed, gusts, dew point risk index, etc.
Geomagnetic activity index affecting GPS accuracy
Sunrise/sunset times and notifications for current location
Copy shapes and various alignment options
Search locations by address and navigation
Real-time data synchronization across multiple devices
Data structure optimized for flight permit applications
Please feel free to contact us with any questions.
Caution and warning icons are for reference only. Always check on-site conditions before flight.
Weather is the most direct factor affecting drone flight safety.
Must consider wind speed, precipitation, visibility, etc. comprehensively
Stop flight immediately if weather conditions deteriorate
Always check weather forecast before flight
Weather information may differ from actual conditions on devices without GPS
Use a device with cellular capability if possible
Weather can change rapidly, so continuous monitoring is necessary even during flight.
Note that forecasts may differ from actual weather
Postpone flight if severe weather is expected
Increased control difficulty, faster battery drain
Recommended for experienced pilots only, watch for gusts

Wind speed is the most important factor for drone flight.

The currently selected %1$s drone can resist wind speeds up to %2$.1fm/s. However, for safety, it is recommended to avoid flying in wind speeds above %3$.1fm/s.

Lighter drones are more affected by wind, so caution is needed even at lower wind speeds.
Wind is stable with minimal fluctuation
Normal flight possible. All maneuvers safe
Increased wind fluctuation may cause unstable drone attitude
Recommended for experienced pilots. Low altitude/short range flight, extra caution during takeoff/landing. Avoid high-speed maneuvers
Sudden wind changes create high risk of attitude loss and collision
Stop or postpone flight immediately. If emergency landing needed, descend very slowly

Gust difference uses DronePass's proprietary calculation formula

① Basic Calculation
Maximum gust speed - Average wind speed = Difference
Example: Gust 10m/s, Average 6m/s → Difference 4m/s

② 4-Axis Simultaneous Evaluation
• Axis A: Gust difference (delta value)
• Axis B: Gust ratio (gust÷average)
• Axis C: Absolute wind speed (average, gust separately)
• Axis D: Aircraft spec limits

③ Customized Thresholds by Drone Weight
Currently selected %1$s drone:
• Caution: %2$.1fm/s or more
• Danger: %3$.1fm/s or more

④ Voting System
Final rating determined by votes from 4 axes
• 2+ danger votes → Danger
• 2+ caution votes → Caution

⑤ Localized Gust Detection
If average wind is very weak (<2.5m/s) but gusts are strong → 🟡 "Localized gust risk" indicator
→ Terrain effects: between buildings, valleys, cliffs
→ Response: Move location or fly only at low altitude (<10m) and short range

⚠️ Special Caution:
• Even if average wind is safe, large difference creates sudden attitude loss risk
• Most dangerous during takeoff/landing (low altitude, possible ground obstacle collision)
• Rapid battery drain (maintaining attitude against strong wind)
• Gusts during high-speed maneuvers can cause path deviation
Light rain, aircraft exposed to moisture
Avoid flight except with waterproof drones
Risk of motor and electronics damage, poor visibility
Most drones are not waterproof. When it rains, the risk of electronic damage is very high, so flight should be avoided.
Limited visibility due to fog, dust, etc.
Cannot secure visibility, difficult to identify obstacles
Visibility is essential for visually confirming the drone and obstacles. Flight should be avoided during fog or yellow dust.
Reduced battery performance, shortened flight time
Rapid battery performance degradation, risk of aircraft damage
Lithium batteries are sensitive to temperature. In extreme temperatures, battery performance degrades rapidly, creating unexpected crash risk.
Air is dry with almost no condensation risk
Normal flight possible (no lens or sensor issues)
High moisture or large temperature difference (60–80%% humidity or 3–6°C temperature difference)
Dew may form on lens or gimbal. Check air flow frequently, avoid long flights or high-altitude flight
Air nearly saturated (80%%+ humidity or 0–3°C temperature difference)
Water droplets form immediately on lens, propellers, sensors. Stop flight or return immediately. Risk of propeller icing below 0°C

Condensation Risk Index uses DronePass's proprietary calculation formula

① Temperature Basis (ΔT Channel)
Checks difference between air temperature and dew point (temperature at which water droplets begin to form).
Smaller difference → Higher condensation risk ↑
Formula: 100 − 10×(Temperature−Dew Point)

② Humidity Basis (RH Channel)
Calculates relative humidity (%%) using Magnus formula.
Higher value → Higher condensation risk ↑

③ Parallel Evaluation
Selects the more dangerous of the two values.

④ Wind Speed Correction
• 5m/s or more: ~20%% reduction
• 2–5m/s: ~10%% reduction
• However, wind effect limited at 90%%+ humidity

⑤ Stabilization
Index stabilized with 5-point moving average

⚠️ Special Caution:
• Temperature difference ≤2°C or humidity 90%%+ → Fog possible, immediate condensation risk
• Below 0°C + humidity 80%%+ → Icing risk! Propellers/sensors may freeze, land immediately
KP Index represents the level of disturbance in Earth\'s magnetic field.
Measures the impact of solar wind and geomagnetic activity
Geomagnetic activity directly affects GPS signal accuracy.
GPS accuracy degradation: Higher KP index reduces GPS signal accuracy
Position tracking errors: GPS-based tracking may fail
KP 5+: Extra caution needed for drone flight
DronePass uses data from two organizations.
GFZ (Germany): Real-time measurements from 13 global stations (3-hour intervals)
NOAA (USA): Real-time estimates + forecasts from 8 stations (minute intervals)
Different number and location of participating stations
Values are usually similar, but may temporarily differ during geomagnetic storms.
Minor geomagnetic storm - Weak power grid fluctuations, minor satellite operations impact
Generally safe, GPS accuracy may slightly decrease
Moderate geomagnetic storm - High-latitude power system voltage alarms, satellite orbit corrections needed
Strong geomagnetic storm - Voltage corrections needed, satellite surface charging and communication interference
Flight caution needed, reduced GPS reliability
Severe geomagnetic storm - Widespread power system problems, satellite tracking and navigation issues
Avoid flight recommended, low GPS reliability
Extreme geomagnetic storm - Possible widespread power grid collapse, satellite communication and navigation failure
